summary: Merge Fleet branch claude/fleet-retention into claude/new-session-2ibknw and deploy: trips, stops, driving events and hourly/daily summaries older than 1 year are deleted for every client, for good (CNDP 17-2014); with the approved clean-up: alerts, fuel events, zone visits and machine sessions keep their record but lose their position after 1 year, driver scores and report files are deleted after 1 year, webhook copies after 30 days
details: Branch at c80c572: the 1-year limit plus the location clean-up, on top of the live fixes (a plain fast-forward, no conflict). Clean-up checked by a plan review and 3 reviewers; their 10 points are fixed, none was serious.

First run: expected to delete or clear close to nothing, because the data starts in August 2026; only records with a wrong tracker date would go. Not checked on the live database: the count queries are in docs/OPERATIONS.md section 4.
Permanent: nothing in the app can bring deleted rows or cleared positions back. The only copy is the backup the deploy takes first; the deploy stops if that backup fails.
Goes slightly beyond "trips, stops and summaries": driving events (harsh braking etc.) are also deleted after 1 year. One line to switch off if you want to keep them.
Backups taken before each deploy are deleted after 30 days (setting BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS on the server).

Users can no longer pick dates older than 1 year in trips, mileage, fuel, analytics, driver scores and the trip/mileage/fuel/driving reports. Old alerts and machine sessions say their position was not kept. The webhook delivery log stops at 30 days.

Production setup change: report files over 8 MiB get their own storage shared by the API and the workers (until now they could not be saved). Could not be built here (no Docker): after the deploy, check that a large report downloads.

Not cleared: anti-theft and out-of-hours records (not in your approval, separate question), delivery records (proofs of delivery, transport orders) and a few technical copies (Redis job history, quarantine files, container logs). Full list in docs/OPERATIONS.md section 4.

Wait for CI to pass first (it needs the GitHub billing fixed): the database parts were run here on a local test database without TimescaleDB, not on the real engine. If it fails on the server, the site stays up on the old version and the deploy needs a manual retry.
Tests: web 1688/1688, API 500 pass (database tests need CI), workers 892 and shared 971 pass; the 2 failing tests already failed before.
After the deploy: add a FAQ entry (draft in products/fleet/changelog.md) and update the privacy page with the sentence in docs/PUBLICATION-STORES.md.
outcome: Approved to go live once CI passes (needs the GitHub billing fixed). Branch now at c80c572, with the approved location clean-up added and pushed.
